method_card.title: Cumulative Frequency and Box Plots
method_card.content:
Cumulative frequency is a running total of frequencies. To build a cumulative frequency table, add each frequency to the running total. The final cumulative frequency must equal the total number of values.

When plotting a cumulative frequency curve, plot each cumulative frequency against the upper boundary of its class (not the midpoint). Join with a smooth S-shaped curve. For discrete data, use a cumulative frequency step polygon: frequency jumps at each exact value.

Reading quartiles from the curve: median at the \(\frac{n}{2}\)th value, Q1 at the \(\frac{n}{4}\)th value, Q3 at the \(\frac{3n}{4}\)th value. Draw a horizontal line from the cumulative frequency, read across to the curve, then drop down to the x-axis.

The interquartile range (IQR) = Q3 − Q1. It measures the spread of the middle 50% and is less affected by extreme values than the full range.

A box plot shows: minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum. When comparing two box plots, always state a numerical comparison of medians and of spreads (range or IQR), then interpret both in context.
steps: Build the cumulative frequency column as a running total
Plot each cumulative frequency against the upper class boundary
Join with a smooth curve (or step polygon for discrete data)
Read the median at n/2, Q1 at n/4, Q3 at 3n/4
For box plot comparison: state median comparison AND spread comparison, both in context

exam_context.marks: 3–6 marks; reading median/Q1/Q3 from a curve is 3 marks; comparing two box plots in context is 3–4 marks
exam_context.frequency: Cumulative frequency curves and box plot comparison appear on almost every paper; IQR and context comparison are the most-tested Higher extensions

worked_examples.question: A cumulative frequency curve shows data for 40 values. At what cumulative frequency should you read to find the median?

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Draw a horizontal line from cumulative frequency = 20 to the curve, then drop down to find the median.

worked_examples.question: A cumulative frequency table for 60 parcels' masses (kg): ≤5: 8; ≤10: 23; ≤15: 44; ≤20: 55; ≤25: 60. Estimate the median mass.

steps.label: Step 1 — Find the median position
steps.content: Median at \(\frac{60}{2} = 30\)th value. cf passes 30 in class ≤15 kg (cf=44 ≥ 30, while cf at ≤10 = 23 < 30).

steps.label: Step 2 — Interpolate within 10–15 kg
steps.content: Need the 30th value. 23 values are ≤10, so the 7th value in the 10–15 class. Class has 44−23=21 values. Estimate: \(10 + \frac{7}{21} \times 5 \approx 11.7\) kg.

worked_examples.question: Two box plots show waiting times at two call centres. Centre A: min 2, Q1 8, median 14, Q3 22, max 35. Centre B: min 1, Q1 5, median 10, Q3 16, max 28. Compare the distributions fully in context.

steps.label: Step 1 — Compare medians
steps.content: A median = 14 min; B median = 10 min. Centre B has shorter typical waits by 4 minutes.

steps.label: Step 2 — Compare IQR
steps.content: A IQR = 22−8 = 14 min. B IQR = 16−5 = 11 min. Centre B is more consistent.

steps.label: Step 3 — Context
steps.content: Centre B provides shorter and more predictable service. Centre A has longer and more variable waits.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Centre B has lower median (10 vs 14 min) and smaller IQR (11 vs 14 min): faster and more consistent for callers.

bronze.display: A cumulative frequency table shows 80 values. At what cumulative frequency do you read to find Q1?
A cumulative frequency table: ≤10: 5; ≤20: 18; ≤30: 34; ≤40: 45; ≤50: 50. What is the cumulative frequency at ≤30?

misconceptions.message: Read the cumulative frequency directly: at ≤30 it is 34. This is a running total.

bronze.display: A box plot shows Q1 = 15 and Q3 = 35. What is the IQR?

misconceptions.message: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 35 − 15 = 20. Do not confuse IQR with range.

bronze.display: A cumulative frequency curve has a maximum of 60. At what cumulative frequency position is Q3?
A box plot for exam scores shows: minimum 30, Q1 48, median 62, Q3 74, maximum 90. What is the range?

misconceptions.message: Range = maximum − minimum = 90 − 30 = 60. Don't use Q3 − Q1 for range.

bronze.display: A cumulative frequency table: ≤150: 4; ≤160: 19; ≤170: 35; ≤180: 46; ≤190: 50. What is the class frequency for the 160–170 interval?

misconceptions.message: Class frequency = difference between consecutive cumulative frequencies: 35 − 19 = 16.

bronze.display: When plotting a cumulative frequency curve for grouped continuous data, points are plotted against which value?
options: The midpoint of the class
The lower class boundary
The upper class boundary
The class frequency

misconceptions.message: Plot cumulative frequency against the upper class boundary. Midpoint is correct for a frequency polygon, not a CF curve.

bronze.display: A box plot has Q1 = 18 and Q3 = 42. Find the IQR.

silver.display: A cumulative frequency table for 40 values: ≤20: 6; ≤30: 18; ≤40: 30; ≤50: 37; ≤60: 40. Estimate the median by interpolation.

misconceptions.message: Median at 20th value. cf at 30 = 18 (< 20); cf at 40 = 30 (≥ 20). Need 2nd of 12 values in class 30–40. Value = 30 + (2/12)×10 ≈ 31.7.

silver.display: Box plot Group X: min 10, Q1 20, median 30, Q3 42, max 60. Box plot Group Y: min 5, Q1 22, median 35, Q3 48, max 65. Which group has the larger IQR?
options: Group X (IQR = 22)
Group Y (IQR = 26)
Both groups have the same IQR
Cannot tell from the box plots

misconceptions.message: IQR X = 42−20 = 22. IQR Y = 48−22 = 26. Group Y has the larger IQR.

silver.display: A cumulative frequency curve for 60 students gives median 54 and Q3 68. At what cumulative frequency value should Q1 be read?
Two box plots compare delivery times. Courier A: median 3 days, IQR 2 days. Courier B: median 4 days, IQR 1 day. A manager wants the most consistent courier. Which should they choose?
options: Courier A — lower median is more consistent
Courier B — smaller IQR means more consistent delivery times
Courier A — lower IQR means more consistent
Courier B — higher median means more reliable

misconceptions.message: Consistency is measured by spread (IQR). Courier B IQR = 1 (smaller) means times cluster more tightly. Courier A is faster on average but less predictable.

silver.display: A cumulative frequency table: ≤5: 3; ≤10: 11; ≤15: 23; ≤20: 31; ≤25: 35. What is the total number of values?

misconceptions.message: The total equals the final cumulative frequency: 35. Do not add all cumulative frequencies together.

silver.display: A box plot shows Q1 = 12, median = 20, Q3 = 31 for 44 students. Find the IQR.

misconceptions.message: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 31 − 12 = 19. Do not include the median.

gold.display: Two schools each have 80 students. School A: median 162 cm, Q1 155 cm, Q3 170 cm. School B: median 165 cm, Q1 160 cm, Q3 172 cm. Which statement gives a full, correct comparison?
options: School B students are taller on average (median 165 vs 162 cm) and slightly more consistent (IQR 12 vs 15 cm). On average, School B students are 3 cm taller.
School A students are taller on average and more varied in height.
Both schools have similar median heights; School B has a larger IQR.
School B is taller but School A is more consistent because it has a larger IQR.

misconceptions.message: IQR A = 170−155=15; IQR B = 172−160=12. B has higher median (taller) and smaller IQR (more consistent). Both comparisons must include context and numbers.

gold.display: A cumulative frequency table for 100 values: ≤10: 8; ≤20: 25; ≤30: 58; ≤40: 82; ≤50: 100. Find Q1 and Q3.

misconceptions.message: Q1 at cf=25: exactly at ≤20 boundary, so Q1=20. Q3 at cf=75: in class 30–40 (cf goes from 58 to 82). Need 17th of 24 values in that class: 30 + (17/24)×10 ≈ 37.1.

gold.display: A cumulative frequency curve for 120 students (exam marks out of 80) gives Q1=38, median=52, Q3=64. The pass mark is 45. Estimate the number of students who passed.

misconceptions.message: Read cf at score=45 from the curve. Interpolate between Q1=38 (cf=30) and median=52 (cf=60): cf ≈ 30 + ((45−38)/(52−38))×30 = 30+15=45. Passed = 120−45=75.

gold.display: Two box plots compare salaries (£000s). Company X: min 18, Q1 24, median 32, Q3 44, max 80. Company Y: min 20, Q1 28, median 36, Q3 46, max 62. Which company offers more consistent salaries?
options: Company X — lower minimum means less variation at the bottom
Company X — larger range is associated with greater consistency
Company Y — smaller IQR (18 vs 20) and smaller range (42 vs 62) both indicate greater consistency
Company Y — higher median automatically means more consistent pay

misconceptions.message: IQR X=44−24=20; IQR Y=46−28=18. Range X=80−18=62; Range Y=62−20=42. Company Y has smaller IQR and smaller range: both measures confirm greater consistency.

gold.display: A cumulative frequency step polygon is drawn for discrete data (absences per student). The cumulative frequency at 2 absences is 31 and at 3 absences is 42. What is the y-value of the step polygon immediately after the step at x = 3?

misconceptions.message: For a step polygon, the y-value after the step at x=3 is the cumulative frequency up to and including 3: which is 42. Before the step, y=31 (cumulative at x=2).
